title: Mission overlay operations
description: The CLOSED set of operations a mission overlay may apply to a mission's JSON before the runtime is built (GH-1394 difficulty postures, GH-1395 challenge amendments: one applier, `applyOverlays` in packages/data/src/overlays.ts). There is no generic 'set any path': every operation names the one field it moves, and none touches tuning, a primary objective's seconds, Conduct scoring, an objective's id, type or target, or a tag. `fail_below` is reached by one operation only, GH-1395's `raise_fail_below`, and only upward. A new operation is a change to this schema AND to the applier's exhaustive switch, made once. Integers and keys only.

oneOf.description: time_limit_s := ceil(time_limit_s * num / den). Only the `withdrawn` backstop moves; a primary's own clock does not.

The mission's enemy wave BODIES scaled by num / den: walking every untagged wave unit in authored order, each entry gets what brings the running total to round-half-up(running authored total * num / den), never below 1 (rounding each entry alone does not keep the ratio: almost every shipped entry is 1 or 2 bodies). A grown entry keeps its count and its extra bodies follow as a second entry at the same spawn point, so the spread never walks off the map. A tagged unit (an eliminate_hvt or locate target) is never scaled: skip_tagged is required and can only be true.
Every clock-timed enemy wave's at_seconds := max(0, at_seconds + seconds). A wave keyed to an objective (`trigger`) does not fire on the clock and is left alone.

Appends one `reinforce` trigger (id `posture_relief`) on `timer_s` at_seconds, bringing `units` in at the map's player_start. A reinforced body is never in the starting-force snapshot, so it moves no credit, and the caller lends it (never joins the roster). label_key is an en.json key; the app resolves it, the harness leaves the trigger unlabelled.
Clears `carries` on every objective: no secondary carries, so the third star and the carried-secondary credit are out of reach (starsFor, creditsFor).

A per-mission amendment (GH-1395 `own`): appends one enemy wave, in mission.schema.json's wave shape (validated there once applied). Amendments run AFTER the posture, so an added wave is never thinned by Easier.

GH-1395 amendment (Clean hands): roe.fail_below := min(80, fail_below + by), so the two-star Conduct floor (fail_below + 20) never passes 100. Only ever UP: a lower floor would pay more Conduct credit (creditsFor reads Conduct over the floor). A mission that declares no fail_below is left alone, and the challenge validator refuses to offer it there.

GH-1395 amendment (Light order, Medics stay back): removes `count` bodies of `unit` from the starting force, from the LAST untagged top-level placements of that unit first; a placement brought to 0 is dropped. A tagged placement is never touched (rule A3), nor a passenger. It only ever lowers creditsFor's `fielded`. Throws when the mission has fewer untagged bodies of `unit` than `count` (an authoring error).

GH-1395 amendment (Thin purse): resources.logistics_start and resources.logistics_rate_per_min := floor(x * num / den), each where declared. Income zones and the supply corridor are untouched. The challenge validator holds num < den.
GH-1395 amendment (No eyes): resources.intel_start := min(intel_start, value), where declared. Only ever down.
